rules.title: Hardcoded secret
rules.description: Passwords, API keys, tokens, private keys, or connection strings with credentials committed in source. Move to a secret store; rotate if already committed.

rules.title: Unsanitized input into an interpreter
rules.description: User-controlled data reaching a command shell, SQL, LDAP, XPath, or template engine without parameterization or escaping. Use the language pack's specific rule when one exists.

rules.title: Unsafe deserialization of untrusted data
rules.description: BinaryFormatter, pickle, Java ObjectInputStream, or eval-style revival of data from requests, files, or queues — remote code execution risk.

rules.title: Weak or misused cryptography
rules.description: MD5/SHA1 for security purposes, DES/RC4, ECB mode, hardcoded IVs/keys, or homegrown crypto. Use modern primitives (AES-GCM, SHA-256+, bcrypt/Argon2 for passwords).

rules.title: User-controlled file path
rules.description: File system paths built from external input without normalization and containment checks — ../../ escapes the intended root.

rules.title: Server-side request to user-controlled URL
rules.description: Server fetches a URL derived from user input without allowlisting — reaches internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.

rules.title: Secrets or PII in logs
rules.description: Credentials, tokens, session ids, or personal data written to logs/telemetry, including in exception messages and debug dumps.

rules.title: Missing authorization check
rules.description: New endpoint, handler, or mutation path with no visible authorization enforcement where sibling operations require it.

rules.title: Mixed-script identifier
rules.description: Identifier mixes scripts with visually confusable characters, which can hide a distinct symbol from reviewers. Replace it with an unambiguous identifier.

rules.title: Confusable keyword
rules.description: Keyword-like token contains characters that look like an ASCII keyword but use another script or compatibility form. Replace it with the intended ASCII spelling.
